newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors to rule on Yeltsin's fitness for surgery.
newsitem.headline: Doctors to rule on Yeltsin's fitness for surgery.

text.p: A council of doctors will determine whether Boris Yeltsin is fit enough to withstand an operation before going ahead with planned heart surgery, a top cardiologist treating the Russian president said on Friday.

"The question of whether the patient's health allows the operation to be carried out is decided by the council," Interfax news agency said, quoting Yevgeny Chazov, the world-renowned specialist who heads Moscow's Cardiological Centre.
Chazov said doctors at his unit had already conducted "coronorography" tests on the president as an out-patient.
These had shown the need for an operation on the blood vessels supplying his heart. Chazov said there was no need to replace any heart valves, as was sometimes necessary.
Some independent medical experts had suggested, on the evidence of wheeziness noted in Yeltsin's television appearances, that he might need treatment for his valves.

Yeltsin indicated in a television interview on Thursday that he planned to have the unspecified heart operation at the Cardiological Centre. The deputy head of another Moscow clinic told Interfax on Friday the operation would be at Chazov's unit.
Chazov, who made his name treating Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev, said the final choice of where to be operated on would be up to Yeltsin, without confirming the choice had been made.
If the president chose the Cardiological Centre, he said, the operation would be performed by professor Renat Akchurin.
